The **DMPG-retningslinjen: Udredning af ADHD hos børn og unge i hospitalsregi og speciallægepraksis** (DMPG Guideline: Assessment of ADHD in children and adolescents in hospital and specialist practice) is a clinical guideline document published in early 2025 [^src1]. It serves as a foundational framework for the assessment of ADHD among younger populations within the Danish healthcare system, specifically standardizing practices in hospital and specialist settings.

The publication of this guideline has had a significant operational impact on national health registries. According to the strategic documentation for the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]], the release of the DMPG guideline in early 2025 secured vital managerial backing to prioritize the specific assessment elements recommended within the document [^src1]. This managerial support is cited as a crucial factor for improving data registration practices and ensuring the fulfillment of national quality indicators across regions.

Furthermore, the guideline directly shapes the specific metrics used to evaluate care quality. The formulation of [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] leans heavily on the DMPG guideline's recommendations, particularly the requirement to gather information about the child's or adolescent's daily life in institutional or school settings [^src2]. The integration of these DMPG guidelines into quality measurement reflects a broader strategic effort to standardize ADHD assessments, address structural barriers in data registration, and align clinical practices with national quality goals.
